reviewer.actual_effort: low; I looked at each of the seven crops once, on my own, and did not open the prior review.json

readings.name: binekha.png
readings.exact_reading: בֵּינְךָ — the nun has a sheva (two dots stacked vertically). The bet has a dagesh and a tsere, and the final kaf has a qamats.

readings.name: hammasakhim.png
readings.exact_reading: כָּל־הַמְּסָכִּים — there is a raised maqaf between כל and ה. The mem has a dagesh dot inside it and a sheva under it.
unresolved: Some vowel marks away from the mem, such as the mark under the ה and the vowels under the samekh and kaf, were not adjudicated. They are outside the target.

readings.name: halleluyah.png
readings.exact_reading: הללויה — ONE yod. This is in the small rubric line ויאמר מזמור קפ״ט הללויה שירו.

readings.name: alah-comma.png
readings.exact_reading: בַּתְּרוּעָה, — a comma is present right after the ה, before the next word.

readings.name: ps47-maqaf.png
readings.exact_reading: כִּי־יְיָ — there is a short horizontal stroke, raised at about the height of the yod tops, between the yod of כי and the Name. It looks like the maqaf in the כָּל־ crop, so I read it as a MAQAF. The Name has a sheva and a qamats underneath.
unresolved: The stroke is clearly there, and its shape and height match a maqaf. But the crop is low resolution, so a print artifact or a merged stroke can't be ruled out completely. My reading leans maqaf from the image alone, not from the familiar Masoretic text.

readings.name: ribbon-comma.png
readings.exact_reading: רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים, בָּנֶיךָ — a comma is present after העולמים.

readings.name: hatori-comma.png
readings.exact_reading: כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה, יוֹם תְּרוּעָה — this is on the lowest row, and a comma is present after בתורה. There is also a comma after הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה on the same row.

limits: I judged only these seven crops. This is not an approval of the whole unit or of the source guidelines.
hatori-comma.png is a wide crop, so the comma after בתורה is small. It is still clearly visible.
ps47-maqaf.png is the only weak point. The Psalm 47:3 maqaf should get a closer look if a sharper scan exists.
